about: Every tool's page in docs/tools/, generated by python -m kit.tooldocs index from the pages; edit the pages, not this file. The standard is docs/TOOL-DOCS.md. Line numbers are 1-based lines of the page.

tools.name: auc
tools.tagline: score an ink map against a segment's published labels
tools.summary: `python -m kit auc` gives the pixel AUC of a 2D ink map against a segment's `inklabels.zarr` inside its `supervision.zarr`, with the reverse-depth map as the control, block-bootstrap intervals, and a paired test of whether one map beats another.

fields.Needs: Python 3.10 or newer, numpy, tifffile (imagecodecs for LZW or zstd TIFFs), zarr (3.x on Python 3.11 or newer; 2.x works for reading)
fields.Runs on: Any CPU. A full-size 5,980 x 8,240 map takes about 5 s with a control and about 6 s with `--bootstrap 300` (measured 2026-10-16, 4-core 2.1 GHz Xeon cloud container, synthetic data)
fields.Writes: Nothing (prints only). With `--slug SLUG`, appends one check to `experiments/SLUG/run.json` (or `ROOT/SLUG/run.json` with `--root`)
fields.Released: Public `main` since 2026-10-07; also inside the AutoPipeline release
fields.Guide: [STANDARDS.md](../STANDARDS.md) (how AUC is used here), [the overlap and baseline log](../logs/2026-10-07-overlap-and-baseline.md) (sampling noise)

tools.name: cli
tools.tagline: the kit command line (python -m kit) and its list of commands
tools.summary: `python -m kit` is the one command line of the workbench: `kit/cli.py` builds a parser of 30 commands (32 actions under eight of them), hands each to its handler, and gives the installed package its four console scripts.

go_ahead.text: Not needed to run the entry point. A command that posts, uploads or rents compute needs Chase's yes first (the go-ahead rule, hard rule 8); its page says so

fields.Run: `python -m kit`, `scrolls-workbench`, `scrolls-letterread`, `scrolls-letterlines`, `scrolls-letterdemo` (the installed package's console scripts), `from kit import cli`
fields.Needs: Python 3.10 or newer (`requires-python` in `pyproject.toml`). The entry point and every module it imports at start are standard library only; a command that needs numpy, tifffile, zarr, Pillow or scipy imports them when it runs (see its page)
fields.Runs on: Any machine. `python -m kit prizes --json` took 0.19 s wall (measured 2026-10-16, cloud container, Python 3.13.16); building the parser once and reusing it brought a repeated `main()` from 13 ms to 2 ms per call (commit `88fbee4`'s message; machine not recorded)
fields.Network: None of its own. Some commands contact hosts (such as `fetch` and `run all --refresh`); each command's page says which
fields.Writes: Nothing of its own. Each command's writes are on its page
fields.Go-ahead: Not needed to run the entry point. A command that posts, uploads or rents compute needs Chase's yes first (the go-ahead rule, hard rule 8); its page says so
fields.Released: Public `main` since 2026-10-06 (`2daee8e`); the console scripts since 2026-10-14 (`2582ab7`)
fields.Guide: [CHANGELOG.md](../../CHANGELOG.md) (what each package version holds and how to install it)

tools.name: compute
tools.tagline: tabulate machine time per run from provenance records
tools.summary: `python -m kit compute` finds the `provenance*.json` records that runs leave behind and prints one row per run with its operator, machine, start time, wall-clock hours and digest, plus an optional energy estimate from an assumed power draw.

fields.Needs: Python 3.10 or newer (`requires-python` in `pyproject.toml`), standard library only. Input: provenance records written by `python -m kit provenance write`
fields.Runs on: Any CPU. Time not measured; two synthetic records returned at once in a cloud container on 2026-10-16
fields.Writes: Nothing (prints only)
fields.Released: Public `main` since 2026-10-07 (`da58d07`)
fields.Guide: [compute.md](../compute.md) (what compute the work needs and what it costs)

tools.name: cropscan
tools.tagline: pixel AUC of one ink map on every window of a grid
tools.summary: `kit.cropscan.scan` scores one ink map against boolean ink and supervision arrays on every full window of a regular grid (by default 640 px windows every 320 px, 64 px edge left out), to show how much a single crop's AUC depends on where the crop was put.

fields.Needs: Python 3.10 or newer, numpy. Labels must already be boolean arrays on the map's grid (for example from `kit.auc.labels_on_map`, which needs zarr)
fields.Runs on: Any CPU. A 4,220 x 4,760 uint8 map (the size of PHerc0841 w00) took 4.1 s for 156 windows, peak process memory 877 MB including the inputs (measured 2026-10-16, 4-core Xeon cloud container, synthetic data). Not faster than scoring each crop directly ([lane I log](../logs/2026-10-07-grok-laneI.md))
fields.Writes: Nothing (returns a list)
fields.Released: Public `main` since 2026-10-07 ([PR #26](https://github.com/ChaseHendrick/Scrolls/pull/26))

tools.name: doctor
tools.tagline: check whether this machine can run villa's First Letters workflow
tools.summary: `python -m kit doctor` checks this machine for what villa's First Letters workflow needs (an NVIDIA GPU with 12 GB, 16 GB of memory, 25 GB of free disk, git, uv and docker, a villa checkout and VC3D's tools) and prints pass, warn or fail for each.

fields.Needs: Python 3.10 or newer, standard library only. Uses `nvidia-smi` (from the NVIDIA driver) when it is on `PATH`, and reads the environment variables `VILLA` and `VC_BIN`
fields.Runs on: Any machine. 0.34 to 0.43 s per call with no `nvidia-smi` installed (5 runs, measured 2026-10-16, 4-core Xeon cloud container). With `nvidia-smi`, add its run time, at most 20 s (the timeout)
fields.Writes: Nothing (prints only). It runs `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,memory.total --format=csv,noheader,nounits` when that program is on `PATH`
fields.Released: Public `main` since 2026-10-06 (`2daee8e`), with the Apple Silicon path since 2026-10-07 (`e8f3dda`). Also inside the AutoPipeline release copy at `faada83`, and as `scrolls-workbench doctor` in the installable package since 2026-10-14 (`2582ab7`)
fields.Guide: [mac.md](../mac.md) (what runs on an Apple Silicon Mac), [compute.md](../compute.md) (hardware that has worked, and the thresholds' sources)

tools.name: ensemble
tools.tagline: average several ink maps of one surface into one map
tools.summary: `python -m kit ensemble` combines two or more ink maps of the same surface on the same grid into one map, by a weighted mean of their scores or of their pixel ranks, keeping out every pixel where any input made no prediction.

fields.Needs: Python 3.10 or newer, numpy; tifffile to read or write `.tif` maps (imagecodecs for LZW or zstd TIFFs). `.npy` in and out needs numpy only
fields.Runs on: Any CPU. Two 600 x 800 maps take about 2 s including start-up; two 4,220 x 4,760 maps (the size of PHerc0841 w00) took 11.9 s with `mean` and 86.4 s with `rank` on a heavily loaded machine (measured 2026-10-16, 4-core 2.1 GHz Xeon cloud container, synthetic maps; see Cost and time)
fields.Writes: The output map `OUT` (`.npy` as float32, anything else as a uint16 TIFF), replacing any file of that name. Nothing else
fields.Released: Public `main` since 2026-10-07 (`ebd4ae3`). The AutoPipeline release package carries its own larger `ensemble` (with a `zscore` method and per-model decoding), described with that release, not here
fields.Guide: [tricks.md](../tricks.md) (map ensembles and z windows, with the community sources and the PHerc0841 numbers)

tools.name: false404-relay
tools.tagline: replay S3's false 404 on chosen zarr chunks, on demand
tools.summary: `scripts/false404/fault_relay.py` is a local HTTP relay in front of the open-data bucket that answers the first GETs of a fixed, seeded share of zarr chunk keys with the 404 `NoSuchBucket` S3 once sent, so VC3D's caching of false 404s (villa #2058) can be shown and its fix tested.

go_ahead.text: Not needed to run it. Posting what it shows, such as a comment or a new render on villa #2058 or #2060, needs Chase's yes (the go-ahead rule, hard rule 8)

fields.Needs: Python 3.10 or newer, standard library only. To show the bug: a VC3D (villa) build that streams zarr volumes over HTTP, pointed at the relay instead of the bucket
fields.Runs on: Any machine; it serves on `127.0.0.1` only. On a fake local bucket it answered 11 requests in about 2.7 s, start and stop included (measured 2026-10-16, cloud container, synthetic data). Speed against the real bucket: Not measured
fields.Network: The upstream it relays to, by default `https://vesuvius-challenge-open-data.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com` (`BUCKET`), one new connection per request; it listens on `127.0.0.1`
fields.Writes: Nothing by default (prints two JSON lines). With `--log LOG`, appends one JSON line per request to LOG
fields.Go-ahead: Not needed to run it. Posting what it shows, such as a comment or a new render on villa #2058 or #2060, needs Chase's yes (the go-ahead rule, hard rule 8)
fields.Released: Public `main` since 2026-10-12
fields.Guide: [the upstream reports log](../logs/2026-10-12-upstream-reports.md) (section 1), [the false-404 receipts](../evidence/2026-10-12-false-404/README.md)

tools.name: fetch
tools.tagline: mirror one folder of the public bucket over HTTPS, resumably
tools.summary: `python -m kit fetch` copies every file under one prefix of the Vesuvius Challenge open-data bucket to a local folder over anonymous HTTPS, with no AWS CLI, and skips files already there at the listed size, so an interrupted fetch resumes.

go_ahead.text: Not needed: anonymous downloads of public data; nothing is posted or rented

fields.Needs: Python 3.10 or newer, standard library only (urllib, concurrent.futures); outbound HTTPS to the bucket. Reading what it fetched needs zarr (the map tools)
fields.Runs on: Any machine with network access. 33 objects (14.7 MB) took 3.9 s and 13 objects (0.12 MB) 6.8 s; a rerun with nothing to download 3.5 s (measured 2026-10-16, 4-core Xeon cloud container behind an HTTPS proxy). A whole surface volume (1.0 to 1.7 GB): Not measured
fields.Network: `vesuvius-challenge-open-data.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com` only (`BUCKET_URL`): S3 ListObjectsV2 listing pages and anonymous GETs of each object. urllib's default opener honours `HTTPS_PROXY`
fields.Writes: The folder `DEST` and every subfolder it needs; one file per bucket object at `DEST/` plus the key minus the prefix, each written first as `NAME.part` and then renamed. Files already there at the listed size are left alone, files of another size are replaced, nothing is deleted
fields.Go-ahead: Not needed: anonymous downloads of public data; nothing is posted or rented
fields.Released: Public `main` since 2026-10-07 (`912135c`); also in the AutoPipeline release copy at `faada83`, and as `scrolls-workbench fetch` in the installed package
fields.Guide: [mac.md](../mac.md) (the w035 download in the Mac runbook)

tools.name: fibertensor
tools.tagline: a retired CPU ink reader built on fibre-orientation features
tools.summary: `python -m kit fibertensor` trains a tiny numpy model on structure-tensor (fibre orientation) and brightness features of one labelled surface-volume window and writes ink maps for others; it was a measured null on public data and is kept so lane D can be rerun.

fields.Run: `python -m kit fibertensor train`, `python -m kit fibertensor predict`, `from kit import fibertensor`
fields.Needs: Python 3.10 or newer, numpy, scipy (`scipy.ndimage`), zarr (3.x on Python 3.11 or newer) to read the volume and labels, tifffile for `predict`. Data: a 9 um surface volume zarr of a labelled public segment and its label folder
fields.Runs on: Any CPU. On a 640 px crop of 28 layers, `train` took 33 s and `predict` 11 s with one BLAS thread (measured 2026-10-16, 4-core Xeon cloud container under load, synthetic data); the lane D log gives about 8 s per pair on Chase's Mac
fields.Writes: `train`: the model at `-o` (numpy adds `.npz` when the name lacks it). `predict`: a float32 TIFF map at `-o`. Both overwrite and print JSON
fields.Released: Public `main` since 2026-10-07 ([PR #14](https://github.com/ChaseHendrick/Scrolls/pull/14)); since 2026-10-14 also in the `scrolls-workbench` package installed from this repository
fields.Replaced by: Nothing. For ink maps use a released ink model such as `ink_9um` or v8in ([v8in-run](v8in-run.md), [mac-w045](mac-w045.md))
fields.Guide: [The lane D log](../logs/2026-10-07-grok-laneD.md) (method, evaluation, result)

tools.name: gate
tools.tagline: rank released ink readers on PHerc0841 by the Gate A rule
tools.summary: `python -m kit gate` ranks ink readers by mean forward AUC on PHerc0841's three standard crops, from the committed CPU scores and any Mac results, requires each crop to beat its reverse-depth control, and says whether the leader wins by Gate A's 0.02 rule.

fields.Needs: Python 3.10 or newer, standard library only. A clone of the repository, because it reads `docs/results.json` (an installed `scrolls-workbench` package does not have it). For Mac rows, the `auc_*.json` files that `scripts/mac-w045.sh` writes
fields.Runs on: Any CPU, about 0.1 s (measured 2026-10-16, 4-core 2.1 GHz Xeon cloud container, committed scores only)
fields.Writes: Nothing (prints only). `scripts/mac-phase0.sh` saves what it prints to `WORK/phase0-gate.txt`
fields.Released: Public `main` since 2026-10-07 (`bec6fb9`). The AutoPipeline release package carries the module (same code, older docstring) but no `gate` command
fields.Guide: [STANDARDS.md](../STANDARDS.md) (the Gate A row and its known gap), [mac.md](../mac.md) (the Phase 0 queue that ends with this table)

tools.name: greeklm
tools.tagline: letter language model for Greek in scriptio continua
tools.summary: `python -m kit greeklm` builds a Kneser-Ney letter n-gram model of Greek written as capitals with no spaces from TEI editions, and scores strings in bits per letter; the letter reader can add a decode with it beside its ink-only letters.

fields.Run: `python -m kit greeklm build`, `python -m kit greeklm score`, `from kit import greeklm`
fields.Needs: Python 3.10 or newer and numpy (the `reader` extra of the `scrolls-workbench` package installs it); Greek TEI XML texts in Unicode, such as the PerseusDL canonical-greekLit editions (CC BY-SA 4.0), fetched by you
fields.Runs on: Any CPU. Building from two Perseus texts (937,054 training letters) took 9.7 s with a peak of 89 MB, and scoring a short string 1.0 s from the command line (measured 2026-10-16, 4-core Intel Xeon cloud container shared with other jobs)
fields.Network: None. It reads local files only; you download the TEI texts yourself
fields.Writes: `build`: the model file OUT, at exactly that path (its folder made if missing), replacing any file there. `score`: nothing (prints only)
fields.Released: Public `main` since 2026-10-14 ([PR #57](https://github.com/ChaseHendrick/Scrolls/pull/57), with the Greek letter reader); in the installable package `scrolls-workbench` since [PR #58](https://github.com/ChaseHendrick/Scrolls/pull/58) the same day
fields.Guide: [letter-reader.md, Optional language model](../letter-reader.md#optional-language-model)

tools.name: hpscore
tools.tagline: letter-scale score of an ink map against a segment's labels
tools.summary: `python -m kit hpscore` correlates an ink map with a segment's published ink labels after removing a 48 um blur from both, so strokes count and blobs do not, with a rolled-label null and an optional reverse-depth control.

fields.Needs: Python 3.10 or newer, numpy, scipy (`scipy.ndimage`), tifffile (imagecodecs for LZW or zstd TIFFs), zarr (3.x on Python 3.11 or newer). The `maps` extra of `pyproject.toml` installs all of them
fields.Runs on: Any CPU. A 640 px crop with its control takes about 0.6 s as a fresh command; a 2,560 px crop about 8 s ([production scaling log](../logs/2026-10-07-production-scaling.md), one core). A full segment has not been measured
fields.Writes: Nothing (prints only). With `--slug SLUG`, appends one check to `experiments/SLUG/run.json` (or `ROOT/SLUG/run.json` with `--root`)
fields.Released: Public `main` since 2026-10-07
fields.Guide: [STANDARDS.md](../STANDARDS.md) (where the letter-scale score sits among the measures), [tricks.md](../tricks.md) (where it came from and what it measured)

tools.name: layers
tools.tagline: export a surface volume to layer TIFFs, and write the depth-shuffle control
tools.summary: `python -m kit layers` writes a surface-volume zarr as numbered layer TIFFs (`00.tif`, `01.tif`, ...), the input v8in reads; `--shuffle SEED`, and `python -m kit shuffle` for a zarr copy, write the depth-shuffle control: the same layers in a fixed random order.

fields.Run: `python -m kit layers`, `python -m kit shuffle`, `from kit import layers`
fields.Needs: Python 3.11 or newer with numpy, tifffile and zarr 3 (checked with numpy 2.5.3, tifffile 2026.10.15, zarr 3.4.1). `kit shuffle` writes with zarr 3's `create_array`, which zarr 2.18 lacks (`pyproject.toml`); `kit layers` only reads zarr. No imagecodecs needed: the TIFFs are zlib-compressed
fields.Runs on: Any CPU. A 28 x 2,048 x 2,048 synthetic volume (117 MB) took 9.7 s to export and 7.2 s to shuffle (measured 2026-10-16, 4-core Xeon cloud container); the whole PHerc0139 w045 volume (28 x 5,980 x 8,240) exported in 23 s (commit `6081aab`, machine not recorded)
fields.Writes: `kit layers`: the folder `OUT_DIR` (created when missing) and one TIFF per layer in it, replacing files of the same names and leaving any other files there. `kit shuffle`: a zarr group at `OUT`; anything already at `OUT` is deleted first
fields.Released: Public `main` since 2026-10-07 (`1caa69e`; the shuffle control since `bd18778`); also in the AutoPipeline release copy at `faada83`

tools.name: letterdemo
tools.tagline: check a letter reader install on synthetic Greek capitals and noise
tools.summary: `python -m kit letterdemo` draws four lines of Greek capitals and a noise image in numpy, reads both with the letter reader's released weights, and prints DEMO PASS or DEMO FAIL under a fixed rule: an offline check that the reader, its weights and numpy work together.

go_ahead.text: Not needed: it downloads public weights and posts nothing

fields.Run: `python -m kit letterdemo`, `scrolls-letterdemo` (the installed package's console script), `from kit import letterdemo`
fields.Needs: Python 3.10 or newer and numpy; Pillow only for the PNG files of `--out`. The reader's weights: a released model (`letters-v2-ccby` by default, 5,933,674 bytes, downloaded once) or a `linenet-v1` `.npz` file. No torch, no GPU, no system font
fields.Runs on: Any CPU. 5.4 s of CPU time with one BLAS thread, 18.5 s wall while other jobs held the 4 cores at a load average of about 14 (measured 2026-10-16, 4-core 2.8 GHz Xeon cloud container, weights cached); the guide measured 6 to 12 s on a 4-core cloud container on 2026-10-14
fields.Network: On the first run only, unless the weights are already in place: the weights download from `github.com`, which redirects to GitHub's release file host (`release-assets.githubusercontent.com` or `objects.githubusercontent.com`). None after that
fields.Writes: The weights file into the cache folder on the first run (`~/.cache/scrolls-kit/letters/`, or `KIT_LETTER_WEIGHTS`). With `--out DIR`: `DIR/demo.json`, and with Pillow `DIR/demo-page.png` and `DIR/demo-overlay.png`, overwritten on a rerun. Otherwise it prints only
fields.Go-ahead: Not needed: it downloads public weights and posts nothing
fields.Released: Public `main` since 2026-10-14 ([PR #58](https://github.com/ChaseHendrick/Scrolls/pull/58)); part of the letter reader release and of the installable package `scrolls-workbench`
fields.Guide: [Check the install: the offline demo](../letter-reader.md#check-the-install-the-offline-demo) in the letter reader guide

tools.name: letterlines
tools.tagline: training lines for the letter reader from your own transcriptions, and their scores
tools.summary: `python -m kit letterlines build` checks records of lines you transcribed and cuts each line as the letter reader sees it into a `LINES.npz` for fine-tuning; `letterlines score` gives one or more models' character error on lines kept apart, with a paired interval.

go_ahead.text: Not needed to run. Lines cut from a text that is not published carry that text: keep their `LINES.npz`, previews and any model trained on them private, and never upload them without Chase's yes (the go-ahead rule, hard rule 8)

fields.Run: `python -m kit letterlines build`, `python -m kit letterlines score`, `scrolls-letterlines` (the installed package's console script), `from kit import letterlines`
fields.Needs: Python 3.10 or newer and numpy; the image libraries the reader loads your images with (tifffile and imagecodecs for TIFF, Pillow for PNG and JPEG, zarr for zarr), which the `reader` extra brings except zarr; Pillow for `--preview`. `score` needs the reader's weights: a released name (downloaded once) or a `linenet-v1` `.npz`. No torch: training on the lines is `scripts/letters/finetune_maps.py`, which needs torch
fields.Runs on: Any CPU, in seconds. On 2026-10-16 (4-core 2.8 GHz Xeon cloud container shared with other jobs, one BLAS thread): a dry run of 4 records in 1.1 s, `build` of 2 lines with a preview in 1.4 s, `score` of 2 lines with two cached models in 1.8 s. The guide measured `build` cutting 54 lines from 9 images in 2.4 s and `score` reading 18 lines with two models in 3.5 s (2026-10-14)
fields.Network: `build`: none. `score`: the first use of a released weights name downloads it from `github.com`, which redirects to GitHub's release file host (`release-assets.githubusercontent.com` or `objects.githubusercontent.com`)
fields.Writes: `build`: the `--out` file (`LINES.npz`) and the `--preview` PNG, making their folders once the records pass; `--dry-run` writes nothing. `score`: the `--out` JSON when given, and the weights file in the cache folder on a released name's first use
fields.Go-ahead: Not needed to run. Lines cut from a text that is not published carry that text: keep their `LINES.npz`, previews and any model trained on them private, and never upload them without Chase's yes (the go-ahead rule, hard rule 8)
fields.Released: Public `main` since 2026-10-14 ([PR #58](https://github.com/ChaseHendrick/Scrolls/pull/58)); part of the letter reader release and of the installable package `scrolls-workbench`
fields.Guide: [Fine-tune on your own lines](../letter-reader.md#fine-tune-on-your-own-lines) in the letter reader guide

tools.name: meshaudit
tools.tagline: audit published cross-scan transforms, meshes and render depth
tools.summary: `python -m kit meshaudit` checks the public catalogue's geometry: it refits each cross-scan affine from its own landmarks, checks each surface volume's canvas against its meshes, picks a seeded set of segments, and measures where the papyrus sits in native and cross-scan renders.

fields.Run: `python -m kit meshaudit transforms`, `python -m kit meshaudit canvas`, `python -m kit meshaudit plan`, `python -m kit meshaudit depth`, `from kit import meshaudit`
fields.Needs: Python 3.10 or newer; numpy for `transforms`, `plan` and `depth`; tifffile (and imagecodecs for LZW meshes) for the mesh functions the study scripts use; zarr only for compressed surface volumes. The rest is the standard library. Checked with Python 3.13 and numpy 2.5
fields.Runs on: Any CPU. `transforms` on the live catalogue took 6 s and `plan` on a local copy 2 s; `canvas` for one scroll (PHerc0841) 17 s, almost all network reads (measured 2026-10-16, 4-core Xeon cloud container, shared). The whole 2026-10-07 study took about an hour on 4 CPUs ([data README](../data/mesh-hypothesis/README.md))
fields.Network: The open-data bucket `vesuvius-challenge-open-data.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com` over plain HTTPS: `metadata.json` (the catalogue, 1.4 MB gzipped) unless `--catalogue` is a local file; for `canvas`, each mesh's `meta.json` and two small range reads of its `x.tif`, and each surface volume's `.zattrs`; for `depth`, the surface volumes' `.zattrs`, `.zarray` and the chunks the tiles touch, from `--base`
fields.Writes: Nothing (prints only). With `--out OUT`, the JSON result to OUT
fields.Released: Public `main` since 2026-10-07 (`e14b033`)
fields.Guide: [The mesh hypothesis protocol](../plans/2026-10-07-mesh-hypothesis.md), [its log](../logs/2026-10-07-mesh-hypothesis.md) and [its data](../data/mesh-hypothesis/README.md)

tools.name: overlap
tools.tagline: do two segments trace the same papyrus, and do their ink maps agree there
tools.summary: `python -m kit overlap` measures how close two tifxyz meshes run (one sheet traced twice, or two surfaces) and how well their human labels agree there against displaced matches; `python -m kit collate` compares two traces' ink maps by gap, against a control.

fields.Run: `python -m kit overlap`, `python -m kit collate`, `from kit import overlap`
fields.Needs: Python 3.10 or newer, numpy, scipy (`cKDTree`, `ndimage.zoom`), tifffile; zarr for `--labels-a` and `--labels-b`; imagecodecs for LZW or zstd TIFF maps. Checked with Python 3.13, numpy 2.5, scipy 1.18, zarr 3.4
fields.Runs on: Any CPU. PHerc0841 w00 against ag896 with labels takes 38 s and 254 MB; a full-size synthetic pair takes 9 s without labels, and `collate` with a control 37 s and 509 MB (measured 2026-10-16, 4-core Xeon cloud container, shared)
fields.Writes: Nothing (prints only)
fields.Released: Public `main` since 2026-10-07 (`25070df`)
fields.Guide: [The overlap and baseline log](../logs/2026-10-07-overlap-and-baseline.md), sections 1, 4 and 6

tools.name: phantom
tools.tagline: synthetic carbon-ink volumes with known truth, to test detectors and AUC noise
tools.summary: `python -m kit phantom` makes small synthetic papyrus surface volumes carrying carbon-ink strokes whose truth is known at every pixel, stress-tests a baseline detector against its depth-reversed control, and compares the AUC spread between phantoms with the one-segment block bootstrap.

fields.Run: `python -m kit phantom`, `bash scripts/phantom-demo.sh`, `from kit import phantom`
fields.Needs: Python 3.10 or newer and numpy (no scipy: the blur is a numpy FFT). `stress` and `calibrate` score with `kit.auc`, which needs only numpy here. The demo script needs bash and must run from the repository root, since it calls `python3 -m kit`
fields.Runs on: Any CPU. `make` at the command's default size (26 x 384 x 384) took 2.1 s, `stress` with its defaults (8 phantoms) 14.2 s, `calibrate` with its defaults 8.2 s, and the whole demo 14.2 s (measured 2026-10-16, 4-core Xeon cloud container)
fields.Writes: `make`: the folder `OUT` (created before the phantom is checked, so it is left empty on a refusal) and `volume.npy`, `ink.npy`, `mask.npy`, `meta.json` in it, replacing earlier ones. `stress --save-maps DIR`: `DIR/surface_SEED.npy` and `DIR/surface_reversed_SEED.npy` per phantom. `calibrate`: nothing. The demo: everything under `$OUT` (default `/tmp/phantom-demo`), listed under Outputs
fields.Released: Public `main` since 2026-10-07 (`eeacf6a`); `kit/phantom.py` is also in the AutoPipeline release copy at `faada83`
fields.Guide: [phantom-and-viewer.md](../phantom-and-viewer.md); results of the demo in the [phantom demo log](../logs/2026-10-07-phantom-demo.md)

tools.name: plan
tools.tagline: print a First Letters run plan for one eligible scroll, and price a run
tools.summary: `python -m kit plan SCROLL` prints the official First Letters commands for one eligible scroll (setup, the w035 control, the w045 labelled check, surface checks, target render and inference, rules before looking) without running them; `python -m kit cost` adds up a run's dollars.

go_ahead.text: Not needed to print a plan or a price. Running its GPU steps on rented compute needs Chase's budget decision (the go-ahead rule, hard rule 8); in this repository GPU work goes to Modal through a run spec (the Modal rule, hard rule 11)

fields.Run: `python -m kit plan`, `python -m kit cost`, `from kit import plan`
fields.Needs: Python 3.10 or newer, standard library only; it reads the prize snapshot through [prizes](prizes.md). The commands it prints need what it does not install: villa, VC3D's tools, uv, the AWS CLI (step 1), huggingface_hub (through `uvx`), and an NVIDIA GPU with CUDA, or an Apple Silicon Mac with `--mac`
fields.Runs on: Any machine. `plan` took 0.11 to 0.49 s and `cost` 0.11 to 0.19 s per call (5 runs each, measured 2026-10-16, 4-core Xeon cloud container). The printed run is another matter: villa's inference on a full segment takes "on the order of an hour on a single GPU" ([tutorial5](https://scrollprize.org/tutorial5))
fields.Network: None. The printed commands, when you run them, reach github.com, huggingface.co and the open-data bucket `s3://vesuvius-challenge-open-data`
fields.Writes: Nothing (prints only). The printed commands write under `villa/vesuvius/` (`checkpoints/`, `ink-dataset/`, `volume-cache/`, `predictions/`, `work/SCROLL_SLUG/`); see Outputs
fields.Go-ahead: Not needed to print a plan or a price. Running its GPU steps on rented compute needs Chase's budget decision (the go-ahead rule, hard rule 8); in this repository GPU work goes to Modal through a run spec (the Modal rule, hard rule 11)
fields.Released: Public `main` since 2026-10-06 (`2daee8e`). Also inside the AutoPipeline release copy at `faada83`, and as `scrolls-workbench plan` and `scrolls-workbench cost` in the installable package since 2026-10-14 (`2582ab7`)
fields.Guide: [WORKFLOW.md](../WORKFLOW.md) (from plan to null or candidate), [mac.md](../mac.md) (the `--mac` path), [compute.md](../compute.md) (hardware and published run costs)

tools.name: prizes
tools.tagline: list the open Vesuvius Challenge prizes from a dated snapshot
tools.summary: `python -m kit prizes` prints each open Vesuvius Challenge prize with its money, deadline, days left and eligible scrolls, from a dated copy of scrollprize.org/prizes kept in `kit/data/`; `--json` prints the copy itself. The live page wins where they differ.

fields.Needs: Python 3.10 or newer, standard library only (json, datetime, pathlib)
fields.Runs on: Any machine. 0.31 to 0.56 s per call for the table and 0.45 to 0.60 s for `--json`, almost all of it Python start-up and importing `kit.cli` (5 runs each, measured 2026-10-16, 4-core Xeon cloud container)
fields.Network: None. It never contacts scrollprize.org: the snapshot is a file in the repository
fields.Writes: Nothing (prints only)
fields.Released: Public `main` since 2026-10-06 (`2daee8e`); the 11 October snapshot since 2026-10-11 ([PR #40](https://github.com/ChaseHendrick/Scrolls/pull/40)). Also inside the AutoPipeline release copy at `faada83`, and as `scrolls-workbench prizes` in the installable package since 2026-10-14 (`2582ab7`)
fields.Guide: [prizes.md](../prizes.md) (the prize terms in prose, from the same snapshot)

tools.name: releases
tools.tagline: keep the README's Released tools section in step with the release list
tools.summary: `python -m kit releases` keeps `docs/releases.json`, the list of tools released from private work into this repository, and writes the README's "Released tools" section from it: pinned entries first, then newest first.

go_ahead.text: Not needed to run it. An entry merged into public `main` is a public release: its exact text is part of the file list Chase approves (the releases rule, hard rule 15), and pushing or merging it needs his yes (the go-ahead rule, hard rule 8)

fields.Kind: kit command, kit module, kit entry point
fields.Run: `python -m kit releases add`, `python -m kit releases render`, `python -m kit releases check`, `python -m kit releases list`, `python -m kit releases pin`, `python -m kit releases unpin`, `python -m kit.releases`, `from kit import releases`
fields.Needs: Python 3.10 or newer, standard library only. A clone of this repository (it reads `docs/releases.json` and `README.md` next to `kit/`), or `--list` and `--readme` pointing at the two files
fields.Runs on: Any machine. `python -m kit releases check` takes about 0.5 s and `python -m kit.releases check` about 0.14 s, almost all of it Python start-up and imports (measured 2026-10-16, 4-core Xeon cloud container, on the 6-entry list)
fields.Network: None. Links in an entry are written into the README, never fetched
fields.Writes: `check` and `list` write nothing. `add`, `render`, `pin` and `unpin` rewrite the release list (`docs/releases.json`, or `--list`) in its written form and the README (`README.md`, or `--readme`) between its two marker lines; the rest of the README is kept byte for byte
fields.Go-ahead: Not needed to run it. An entry merged into public `main` is a public release: its exact text is part of the file list Chase approves (the releases rule, hard rule 15), and pushing or merging it needs his yes (the go-ahead rule, hard rule 8)
fields.Released: Public `main` since 2026-10-14 ([PR #60](https://github.com/ChaseHendrick/Scrolls/pull/60)); pins since 2026-10-14 ([PR #83](https://github.com/ChaseHendrick/Scrolls/pull/83)). Scrolls-private's submission exporter carries an identical copy of the module
fields.Guide: [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md) (the releases rule, hard rule 15, and the standing decisions of 14 October 2026)

tools.name: rowscore
tools.tagline: text-row periodicity triage score for ink maps
tools.summary: `python -m kit rowscore` measures how strongly an ink map repeats at a 2.5 to 8 mm period in one direction, as rows of Greek text do, for forward and reverse maps: a triage aid that says where to look first, not a verdict.

fields.Needs: Python 3.10 or newer, numpy, tifffile (imagecodecs for LZW or zstd TIFFs); scipy for the largest-piece step (skipped without it) and for `--fast-resize`
fields.Runs on: Any CPU. A 305-million-pixel public map took 39.7 s, or 5.7 s with `--fast-resize` ([production scaling log](../logs/2026-10-07-production-scaling.md), one core); a 9 um segment takes seconds to under a minute
fields.Writes: Nothing (prints only). With `--slug SLUG`, appends one check to `experiments/SLUG/run.json` (or `ROOT/SLUG/run.json` with `--root`)
fields.Released: Public `main` since 2026-10-07
fields.Guide: [rowscore.md](../rowscore.md) (the `--fast-resize` option and its numerical limits)

tools.name: run-ledger
tools.tagline: the local experiment ledger, one run.json per experiment
tools.summary: `python -m kit run init`, `status`, `cost`, `record`, `check` and `list` keep one `run.json` per experiment under `experiments/`: the question, a readout rule hashed before any output is seen, a status that cannot jump to published, costs, file hashes and checks.

go_ahead.text: Not needed to keep the ledger. Moving a record into git, or making a `candidate` or `submitted` one public, is never allowed before the official announcement (the no-findings rule, hard rule 1)

fields.Run: `python -m kit run init`, `python -m kit run status`, `python -m kit run cost`, `python -m kit run record`, `python -m kit run check`, `python -m kit run list`, `from kit import ledger`
fields.Needs: Python 3.10 or newer, standard library only. `run init` reads the dated prize snapshot `kit/data/prizes-2026-10-11.json` through `kit/prizes.py`
fields.Runs on: Any CPU. Each action took about 0.13 s wall on a one-record ledger, almost all of it Python start-up (measured 2026-10-16, 4-core cloud container, synthetic record). `run record` hashes every `--file` in full, so it grows with file size; not measured on large files
fields.Writes: `experiments/SLUG/run.json` (or `ROOT/SLUG/run.json` with `--root`): `init` creates it and its folder; `status`, `cost` and `record` rewrite it in place. `check` and `list` write nothing
fields.Go-ahead: Not needed to keep the ledger. Moving a record into git, or making a `candidate` or `submitted` one public, is never allowed before the official announcement (the no-findings rule, hard rule 1)
fields.Released: Public `main` since 2026-10-06 (`2daee8e`)
fields.Guide: [WORKFLOW.md](../WORKFLOW.md) (plan, run, null or candidate, with these commands)

tools.name: soup
tools.tagline: average the weights of several checkpoints of one training run
tools.summary: `scripts/soup.py` writes a checkpoint soup, the uniform mean of the weights of two or more checkpoints from one training run (such as `ink_9um` seed 42 at steps 40k to 75k), and refuses checkpoints whose `config.seed` differs, because a cross-seed weight average breaks the model.

go_ahead.text: Not needed to make a soup. Uploading one (such as to Hugging Face) needs Chase's yes first (the go-ahead rule, hard rule 8)

fields.Tests: None: no test in `tests/` runs it. The saved one-off check `scripts/experiments/2026-10-07-cloud/tricks/soup_check.py` compared its output with Nieuwlaar's published soup (see Checks and controls)
fields.Needs: Python 3 and PyTorch (`torch`), which the script imports at the top, so even `--help` fails without it. The 2026-10-07 run used Python 3.14 and torch 2.14.1+cpu (`scripts/experiments/2026-10-07-cloud/tricks/notes.md`). Checkpoints saved with `torch.save`
fields.Runs on: Any CPU; every tensor is loaded with `map_location="cpu"` and nothing uses a GPU. Wall time Not measured: the 2026-10-07 soup of four `ink_9um` checkpoints recorded no time
fields.Network: None. Downloading the checkpoints is a separate step (Quick start)
fields.Writes: The file `OUT` (replaced if it exists), nothing else
fields.Go-ahead: Not needed to make a soup. Uploading one (such as to Hugging Face) needs Chase's yes first (the go-ahead rule, hard rule 8)
fields.Released: Public `main` since 2026-10-07 (`ebd4ae3`)
fields.Guide: [tricks.md](../tricks.md) (the community tricks, with the soup's measured numbers)

tools.name: stackcheck
tools.tagline: check consecutive segments of one scroll against its umbilicus, from geometry alone
tools.summary: `python -m kit stackcheck` checks a stack of consecutive tifxyz segments, inner to outer, against the scroll's umbilicus: winding order, coincident or oddly spaced pairs, missing sectors and runs, skipped windings, turn overlaps and stack ends, with masks of the flagged vertices.

fields.Needs: Python 3.10 or newer, numpy, scipy (`cKDTree`, `ndimage.label`), tifffile. Inputs: the segments' tifxyz folders and the scroll's published umbilicus JSON. Checked with Python 3.13, numpy 2.5, scipy 1.18
fields.Runs on: One CPU core. PHerc0139 run A (5 segments) took 49.8 s and 0.75 GB, run B (18 segments) 144.8 s and 1.7 GB (`stackcheck_checks` in `results.json`, 2026-10-14); a synthetic six-winding stack takes 13 to 16 s and 166 MB (measured 2026-10-16, 4-core Xeon cloud container, shared)
fields.Network: None for local folders. For `https://` or `s3://` segments, the umbilicus or the catalog: the open-data bucket `vesuvius-challenge-open-data.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com` (or the host the URL names), for each segment's `x.tif`, `y.tif`, `z.tif` and `meta.json`, the umbilicus JSON, and `metadata.json` for `--transform catalog:...` without a local `--catalog`
fields.Writes: Fetched segments under `--cache` (default `work/stackcheck/cache/HOST/PATH/`, kept for reuse); the JSON report with `--out`; the masks `.npz` with `--flags`. Otherwise it prints only
fields.Released: Public `main` since 2026-10-14 (`47cd607`); listed in the README's "Released tools" as the release `stackcheck` (Segment stack check)
fields.Guide: [The PHerc0139 segment note](../logs/2026-10-14-pherc0139-segment-defects.md): usage, the PHerc0139 numbers, example vertices for VC3D, a look at the CT and the limits

tools.name: surfacefix
tools.tagline: suggest bounded normal shifts of a surface from two traces' ink maps
tools.summary: `python -m kit surfacefix` writes copies of a traced surface shifted along its normal, then, from one ink model's maps of those copies and of a second trace of the same sheet, flags regions where the traces disagree and copies only control-passing shifts into a new surface.

go_ahead.text: Not needed to run it. The renders and model runs it needs happen outside it; GPU inference goes to Modal (the Modal rule, hard rule 11)

fields.Run: `python -m kit surfacefix prepare`, `python -m kit surfacefix apply`, `from kit import surfacefix`
fields.Needs: Python 3.10 or newer, numpy, scipy (`cKDTree`, `map_coordinates`, `gaussian_filter`), tifffile (imagecodecs for compressed TIFF maps). The ink maps come from outside: villa's `vc_render_tifxyz` to render each mesh and an ink model run three ways on each render
fields.Runs on: Any CPU. `prepare` on a 32 x 32 vertex mesh took 0.6 s; `apply` on that mesh with 320 x 320 maps took 2.3 s of CPU (3.5 to 6.8 s wall on a busy machine), and on a 64 x 64 mesh with 640 x 640 maps 6.9 s of CPU (measured 2026-10-16, 4-core Xeon cloud container, synthetic data). The real 32 x 32 PHerc0841 crop took a median 2.28 s on one core ([production scaling log](../logs/2026-10-07-production-scaling.md))
fields.Writes: `prepare`: a new folder OUT with `manifest.json` and one `offset-NNN.tifxyz/` per offset. `apply`: a new folder OUT with `corrected.tifxyz/` and `report.json`. Both refuse an OUT that exists or overlaps an input; inputs are never changed
fields.Go-ahead: Not needed to run it. The renders and model runs it needs happen outside it; GPU inference goes to Modal (the Modal rule, hard rule 11)
fields.Released: Public `main` since 2026-10-07 ([PR #17](https://github.com/ChaseHendrick/Scrolls/pull/17))
fields.Guide: [surfacefix.md](../surfacefix.md) (workflow, acceptance checks, validation scope)

tools.name: v8in-run
tools.tagline: run the v8in ink model on a layer folder, with opt-in fp16 on the Mac GPU
tools.summary: `scripts/v8in_run.py` runs Youssef Nader's v8in ink model, or its PHerc1447 fine-tune, on a folder of numbered layer images and writes one ink probability map, with an optional fp16 autocast on Apple's MPS GPU and a final log line the Mac scripts parse.

go_ahead.text: Not needed for a local run on public data. Renting a GPU for it on Modal needs Chase's yes and a run spec (the go-ahead rule, hard rule 8, and the Modal rule, hard rule 11)

fields.Tests: None: no test in `tests/` runs it. Its end-to-end check is the CPU against MPS crop comparison in `scripts/mac-w045.sh` (step 5, `kit verify` with the reverse map as the control)
fields.Needs: Python 3 with the packages of v8in's `requirements.txt`: torch 2.1 or newer, numpy, tifffile, imagecodecs, opencv-python-headless, safetensors, huggingface_hub 0.25 or newer (the runs here used torch 2.14.1). A local snapshot of the model repository, `YoussefMoNader/ink-8um-v8in` at `d89166b` (MIT, `model.safetensors` 333,532,180 bytes) or `YoussefMoNader/ink-8um-v8in-pherc1447-loo-w062` at `2bf9f42`. `--fp16` needs an Apple Silicon Mac with MPS
fields.Runs on: CPU, Apple MPS or CUDA. About 8 s per tile on 4 CPU cores of a Linux container (base v8in; [community scan log](../logs/2026-10-07-community-scan.md)) and 7.4 s per tile for the fine-tune (196 tiles in 1,444 s, `scripts/experiments/2026-10-07-cloud/v8in1447-w00/notes.md`); on Chase's M1 Pro, 1.1 to 1.2 s per tile on MPS in fp32, 5.5 to 6.2 s in fp16, and 25 s on its CPU ([mac.md](../mac.md)). All 2026-10-07. Whole segments are GPU jobs
fields.Network: None. The model loads from the local `--model-dir`; downloading that snapshot from huggingface.co is a separate step
fields.Writes: The map at `--output` (replaced if it exists) and any missing parent folders. Progress and the final line go to stdout
fields.Go-ahead: Not needed for a local run on public data. Renting a GPU for it on Modal needs Chase's yes and a run spec (the go-ahead rule, hard rule 8, and the Modal rule, hard rule 11)
fields.Released: Public `main` since 2026-10-07 (`6081aab`)
fields.Guide: [mac.md](../mac.md) (the Mac runs that call it, with their times)

tools.name: verify
tools.tagline: check that two ink maps of the same input agree, with a control
tools.summary: `python -m kit verify` compares a candidate ink map (such as an Apple GPU run) with a reference map (such as the CPU run) pixel by pixel, and counts agreement as a pass only when a control map that should differ is caught by the same test.

go_ahead.text: Not needed to run it. Posting its output, for example on a villa PR, needs Chase's yes (the go-ahead rule, hard rule 8)

fields.Needs: Python 3.10 or newer, numpy, tifffile; imagecodecs for LZW-compressed TIFFs, which is how villa writes its maps. villa's environment has all three
fields.Runs on: Any CPU. A 2.4 um w035 ink map of 22,640 x 20,400 px with a control took 36 s and 2.25 GB ([mac.md](../mac.md#runbook-verify-mps-against-cpu-on-the-control-segment), 2026-10-07); a 5,980 x 8,240 uint8 map with a control took 17 s and 512 MB (measured 2026-10-16, shared 4-core cloud container, synthetic maps)
fields.Writes: Nothing (prints only). With `--slug SLUG`, appends one check to `experiments/SLUG/run.json` (or `ROOT/SLUG/run.json` with `--root`)
fields.Go-ahead: Not needed to run it. Posting its output, for example on a villa PR, needs Chase's yes (the go-ahead rule, hard rule 8)
fields.Released: Public `main` since 2026-10-07
fields.Guide: [mac.md, "Runbook: verify MPS against CPU on the control segment"](../mac.md#runbook-verify-mps-against-cpu-on-the-control-segment)

tools.name: view
tools.tagline: one offline HTML page that overlays several ink maps and the labels
tools.summary: `python -m kit view` writes one self-contained HTML file (no server, no network) that shows several readers' ink maps of one crop, percentile ranked so different scales compare, with their disagreement, the label outline and the mask, plus a JSON summary.

go_ahead.text: Not needed to build a page. Posting or sending the page to anyone is an outward action that needs Chase's yes (the go-ahead rule, hard rule 8), and a page built from a target-scroll map is never shared or committed (the no-findings rule, hard rule 1)

fields.Needs: Python 3.10 or newer, numpy; tifffile for `.tif` maps (imagecodecs too for LZW or zstd TIFFs). A web browser with JavaScript to open the page; nothing else
fields.Runs on: Any CPU. Two 256 x 256 maps take about 1 s; three full-size 5,980 x 8,240 float32 maps with labels and mask take about 11 s and 765 MB peak memory (measured 2026-10-16, 4-core Xeon cloud container under load from other jobs, synthetic data)
fields.Network: None. The page loads nothing: every image is a PNG data URI inside the file
fields.Writes: `OUT.html` (overwritten if it exists); with `--png PNG`, that PNG file. Prints a JSON summary to stdout
fields.Go-ahead: Not needed to build a page. Posting or sending the page to anyone is an outward action that needs Chase's yes (the go-ahead rule, hard rule 8), and a page built from a target-scroll map is never shared or committed (the no-findings rule, hard rule 1)
fields.Released: Public `main` since 2026-10-07 ([PR #13](https://github.com/ChaseHendrick/Scrolls/pull/13)); since 2026-10-14 also in the `scrolls-workbench` package installed from this repository, as `scrolls-workbench view`
